result.title: GEAR: Generative Editing for Scene-Conditioned Outfit Retrieval for VR Travel
result.summary: In virtual environments, choosing appropriate outfits requires contextual harmony with surrounding scenes, yet bridging the visual gap between 3D ambient views and catalog garment assets remains challenging. This paper investigates scene-conditioned outfit retrieval for interactive 3D environments, where a user's egocentric view serves as the retrieval signal. We present GEAR (Generative Editing for Asset Retrieval), a framework that bridges the cross-domain gap by synthesizing intermediate visual queries rather than predicting direct compatibility. GEAR uses a vision-language model to describe suitable clothing from a captured scene, employs an instruction-guided diffusion model to render the concept onto a standardized reference character, and utilizes the cropped clothing region to retrieve existing 2D outfit assets via embedding similarity. An interactive Unity prototype demonstrates real-time scene capture, asset retrieval, and in-engine 3D avatar fitting. We benchmark GEAR against direct visual similarity, aesthetic scoring, and VLM-based reranking on a controlled dataset using automated Swiss-system pairwise judgments, where GEAR achieves competitive top-ranked performance (mean Elo@5 of 1012.75 and top-10 overlap of 0.180) alongside 0.539 pairwise agreement. Furthermore, a user study across 20 virtual travel scenes demonstrates that GEAR achieves the highest overall participant preference in both visual appeal (34.5%) and contextual suitability (34.5%).

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向 VR 旅行场景提出 GEAR：由视觉语言模型描述场景适配服饰，用指令引导扩散模型在标准角色上渲染服饰概念，再裁剪服装区域做嵌入相似度检索，并在 Unity 原型中实现实时捕捉与 3D 换装。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于场景条件化服饰检索的 VR 应用系统，中间生成步骤只是构造跨域检索查询，不涉及推理期状态生成与更新、视觉证据筛选、停止决策或 latent 使用的训练监督，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
